newsitem.title: KYRGYZSTAN: Kyrgyzstan to privatise promising energy sector.
newsitem.headline: Kyrgyzstan to privatise promising energy sector.

text.p: Kyrgyz President Askar Akayev has ordered the government to work out by April 1 plans for privatising the country's promising energy sector.

A presidential decree published in local newspapers on Monday said corporate management was being imposed on the state energy company Kyrgyzenergoholding as a first step in privatisation, and a board of directors was being set up.
The board of directors will have to work out the strategy for privatising the energy sector. Vice-president Kudaikul Abasbekov has been appointed acting chief executive of Kyrgyzenergoholding.

Officials and newspapers have not said which foreign or local companies are interested in buying local power stations but the energy sector could become one of the most attractive investments in the former Soviet republic.
The decree exempted from privatisation only five hydro-electric power stations situated on the mountainous Toktogul cascade of the Naryn river.

Kyrgyzstan, with 19 hydro-electric power stations and two thermal ones, produces annually 12-14 billion kilowatt/hours, making use of just nine percent of its huge energy potential, estimated at 142.5 billion kilowatt/hours.
Energy output was 10.96 billion kwh in January-October 1996, according to official statistics.
The country exports electricity to two other Central Asian states, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.
In 1994-1996 Kyrgyzstan exported to Kazakhstan 4.7 billion kwh and another 1.0 kwh to Uzbekistan for a total of $179.4 million.
